Implement a standalone OrderRegister that records supplied order totals and
tracks whether each order has been dispatched.

A newly created register contains no orders. order_count() returns the number
of registered orders.

create_order(order_id, total_price) creates an order with the supplied identifier
and total price. A newly created order has status "pending".

order_total(order_id) returns the total price supplied when the order was created.
order_status(order_id) returns either "pending" or "dispatched".

dispatch_order(order_id) changes an existing pending order to "dispatched".
Dispatching an already dispatched order leaves it dispatched. Dispatching an
order must not change its total, the order count or any other order.

Creating an order with an identifier that already exists raises ValueError.
The existing order and all other register contents remain unchanged.

Querying the total or status of an unknown order, or attempting to dispatch an
unknown order, raises KeyError and leaves the register unchanged.

Reading order totals, statuses or the order count does not change the register.
Separate OrderRegister instances hold independent state.

For this behavior, valid order identifiers are non-empty strings and valid total
prices are non-negative integers representing minor currency units. Zero is a
valid total. Other input types or values are outside the specified input domain;
do not invent additional validation or exception requirements for them.

For example, create_order("order-001", 500) creates one pending order with total
500. Creating "order-002" with total 200 makes the count 2. Dispatching "order-001"
changes only its status: its total remains 500, the count remains 2, and
"order-002" remains pending with total 200.

The register is standalone, dependency-free and in memory. It accepts supplied
order identifiers and totals. It does not calculate basket totals, retrieve
catalogue products, generate identifiers, process payments or contact external
services.
